To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
participatory mental consumer research for physical health in mental illness has only recently emerged and that mental health nurses can play an important role in facilitating such research.

The current review found that participative mental health consumer researchers in four studies identified barriers to accessing physical healthcare, and that mental health consumers can contribute to research that improves physical health care.
mental health consumers can be involved in research to improve physical health care, but this is currently underrepresented in the research literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health of people with mental illness, who are at risk of dying prematurely due to the poor quality of their care.
the development of a new theory of mental health nursing, which is based on the concept of mental health recovery.
understanding the experiences of mental health service consumers in accessing physical healthcare, and the barriers and facilitators that influence the quality of their physical health care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are few examples of mental health consumer focussed research on physical health care, and that mental health consumer involvement in research is an underutilised and potentially powerful strategy to improve physical health care in mental health services.
mental health consumer participation is essential in research to improve physical health care.

mental health consumers have been involved in physical healthcare research in the context of a mental health service in the past 10 years and this is a new and developing area of mental health consumer research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mental health consumers are not only the most important people to be involved in mental health care research, they are also the best people to lead the research.
the mental health consumer is an important stakeholder in the development of physical health care for people with mental health problems.
mental health consumers are a vital source of knowledge for improving physical health outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mental health consumer researchers are a valuable resource for improving the quality of mental health services and the health outcomes of consumers.
the inclusion of consumers as co-researchers is a promising approach to improving physical health care for mental health consumers.
mental health consumers are a rich source of knowledge for health care reform.
